subject: Request: keystore retention window & targeted log-sampling for NimbusCloud legal hold
messages:
From: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimbuscloud.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Keystore deletion window + targeted log sampling — Nimbus legal hold

Hi Olga,

We're working through an internal legal hold for a small set of tenant IDs (see attached Nimbus_LegalHold_20271028.pdf). The hold requires us to preserve any customer-specific cryptographic material and audit trails tied to the affected tenants through the end of the investigation. Our compliance team flagged two items where we need clarity from Redwood before we can complete our evidence packet:

1) Keystore deletion/rotation windows: your SOC 2 materials indicate automatic deletion of expired keys after rotation. Can Redwood provide an option to suspend deletion for a scoped set of tenant keystore records (tenant IDs listed in the attachment) for up to 120 days? If a full suspension isn't feasible, what is the minimum operational window you can guarantee and what evidence can be exported to attest that those keys were preserved (hashes, stubs, timestamps)?

2) Log and KV-cache sampling: we need a targeted export of audit logs + any KV-cache metadata that might include key lookup references for the affected tenants. We don't need full session payloads; a narrow audit trace that includes timestamps, operations, and referencing IDs would be sufficient. Can you confirm retention windows and whether Redwood can deliver a time-bounded export scoped to the tenant IDs listed?

Please advise on technical feasibility, proposed controls (PII minimization, redaction or hashing), and an estimated timeline. We're under a hard deadline to include Redwood's response in our legal packet by Nov 10.

Thanks — appreciate the quick turn.

Evan Brooks
Security & Compliance Lead
NimbusCloud
Attachments: Nimbus_LegalHold_20271028.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@nimbuscloud.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@nimbuscloud.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Nov 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Keystore deletion window + targeted log sampling — Nimbus legal hold

Evan — thanks for the note and the attachment. I've looped in Karthik (security/infra) and Marissa (CS) so we can scope a safe, auditable response. High-level initial thoughts:

- We can support a scoped, tenant-specific preservation for keystore records but we need to lock down exactly which artifacts you require (full keys vs. key metadata/hashes). Full key suspension has operational & security implications, so our default is to preserve key metadata and a HMAC-hashed reference to the key material rather than suspending deletion of raw keys.

- For logs and KV-cache traces we can produce a time-bounded export limited to the tenant IDs you provided. We routinely rotate ephemeral caches; we can capture audit logs (control-plane + key-management audit events) and a small sampled KV metadata export that contains lookup references (hashed) and timestamps — not full payloads.

Action items for Nimbus: please confirm the tenant IDs (you provided abbreviated IDs in the PDF — full tenant UUIDs or account IDs will help) and whether legal requires raw keys or whether hashed attestations + preserved audit trails are sufficient.

Proposed Redwood deliverable (if you confirm hashed attestations are acceptable):
- Scoped keystore-preservation flag for listed tenant UUIDs for 90 days (provisionally)
- Time-bounded audit export (control-plane audit events + KM operations) covering the retention window
- Sampled KV metadata export: hashed references, operation type, timestamps
- Signed attestation from Redwood security describing the preservation steps and hashes provided

I've attached a short spreadsheet with our proposed scope and minimal data elements we'd export (proposed_scope_keystore_retention.xlsx). Once you confirm, Karthik will validate technical feasibility and we'll surface any changes to timeline or privacy controls.

We should be able to turn around an initial export and attestation in 5–7 business days after scope confirmation, subject to legal review on both sides. If you need an extension beyond 90 days, we'll need a formal exception request and an authorization from Nimbus legal (cc: Priya).

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Enterprise Customer Security (acting)
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Keystore deletion window + targeted log sampling — Nimbus legal hold

Evan / Priya — quick technical note from infra/security on how we can support the request and the trade-offs.

1) Keystore preservation options:
   - Full key suspension: we can flip a tenant-specific preservation flag that prevents routine deletion/rotation for specified key records. This is possible but increases the attack surface and complicates rotation semantics; engineering will require an authorization ticket and a narrow time-box (we recommend <= 120 days).
   - Hashed attestations (preferred): we produce signed HMACs of key material (we never expose raw keys in exports) plus key metadata (creation time, rotation timestamp, key-id). The HMAC approach lets you prove existence without handing over raw material.

2) Logs & KV-cache exports:
   - Control-plane audit logs (create/delete/rotate/key-access) are fully available for the requested window; retention default is 90 days for audit logs but we can export historical slices earlier than automatic purge if the window overlaps current data.
   - KV cache (in-memory) is ephemeral; any lookup references that hit persistent indices are recorded in our audit logs. We can also provide a limited sampled export that lists hashed lookup keys and operation types (GET/SET/DELETE) with timestamps. This will not contain application payloads.

3) Data minimization & evidence format:
   - Exports will be CSV/NDJSON with SHA-256/HMAC hashed identifiers. We can include a manifest and a signed attestation describing the transform and salt used (salt stored only by Redwood security).

4) Timeline & costs:
   - Once scope is confirmed, engineering can produce the export and attestation within 3–5 business days for a single 30–90 day window; larger windows or requests for raw keys will require additional review and a formal exception ticket (SEC-9742).

Next steps from Redwood: confirm exact tenant UUIDs, confirm acceptance of hashed attestations vs raw keys, and confirm desired preservation window (90 vs 120 days). If you authorize full key suspension we will require a signed DPA addendum and Redwood legal approval.

I've attached a small schema describing the export layout for the KV metadata — kv_export_schema.json — for your compliance team to review.

Thanks,
Karthik
Principal Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: kv_export_schema.json (application/json)

Olga / Karthik — thanks for the quick responses and the proposed scope. Per our legal team: hashed attestations + preserved audit trails are acceptable for the current investigation, provided Redwood includes a signed attestation and an export manifest that documents the hashing/HMAC process.

Nimbus asks for the following to proceed:
- Preservation window: please set the scoped preservation flag for the listed tenant UUIDs for 90 days starting today (Nov 4).
- Deliverables: time-bounded control-plane audit export + sampled KV metadata (hashed IDs) covering Oct 20–Nov 4, and a signed attestation describing the transforms.
- Authorization: Priya (cc'd) will send a signed authorization email; if you need an addendum to the DPA for a key suspension beyond hashed attestations we'll coordinate that separately.

Can you confirm you received Priya's authorization and provide an estimated completion timestamp? We need the export + attestation to include in the legal hold packet by Nov 10.

I'll attach a short confirmation file for our records. Thanks again for the quick collaboration.

Evan Brooks
